We were concerned that there was no disclosure of performance targets which determine vesting of the Long Term Incentive Plan. We were concerned regarding the pay for performance alignment. Concerns have been identified with the departing CEO's exit arrangements, in particular the Company's decision to pro-rate his outstanding LTIP awards until after his retirement date and following a further 12 month period during which time he will provide advisory services to the Company. Furthermore, the Company has chosen to accelerate vesting of these awards to 30 June 2024 and estimate the performance for the ensuing year in determining the amount that should vest. Lastly, he is not subject to the post-vesting holding period for the LTIP awards. The incoming CEO received a one-off exceptional award to incentivise a strategic initiative.

We have concerns regarding the significant vesting outcome of the 2021 Long Term Incentive Plan. While we recognise that there was no significant reduction in share price between the awards granted May and June 2021, we have concerns that the company reverted to a 300% of salary incentive award and there was no subsequent adjustment on vesting for windfall gains despite the depressed share price at grant. We additionally have concerns regarding the reputational impact of such a significant award.

Concerns regarding the one off Long Term Incentive award of 16x salary. In addition this award is determined wholly by relative TSR with no formal financial underpin. Consistent with our votes last year we consider a vote against to be appropriate.

AllianzGI believes that all incentive awards should be time pro-rated and tested for performance, including in the event of an early termination due to the change of control. Termination payments following a change of control should be similar to those available under normal circumstances. AllianzGI expects clear disclosure of KPIs under all management incentive plans to enable investors to better assess the link between management incentives and corporate strategy and performance.
AllianzGI encourages companies to include ESG KPIs in their remuneration policy.

A substantial proportion of annual remuneration should be provided as shares that are locked in for five to ten years, regardless of resignation or retirement.
